notes.title: HTML
notes.description: The skeleton of every webpage. Defines structure and content using tags and elements.

notes.title: CSS
notes.description: Controls how things look on screen — colors, layouts, spacing, and responsiveness.

notes.title: JavaScript
notes.description: The programming language of the web. Makes pages interactive and dynamic.

notes.title: DOM
notes.description: How JavaScript talks to the webpage. Read, change, and react to HTML in real time.

notes.title: Node.js
notes.description: Lets you run JavaScript outside the browser — on servers, scripts, and tools.

notes.title: Express
notes.description: A lightweight framework for building web servers and APIs with Node.js.

notes.title: EJS
notes.description: A templating language that lets you generate HTML with JavaScript on the server.

notes.title: API
notes.description: How apps talk to each other. Send requests, get data back, connect services.

notes.title: SQL
notes.description: The language used to create, read, update, and delete data in databases.

notes.title: Git & Bash
notes.description: Track your code changes and work with the terminal like a developer.

notes.title: GitHub
notes.description: Where your code lives online. Collaborate, share, and manage projects.

notes.title: Bash Shortcuts
notes.description: Custom terminal shortcuts to speed up repetitive commands.

notes.title: Web Design
notes.description: The art side of building websites — how to make things look good and feel right.

notes.title: Backend
notes.description: The big picture of what happens behind the scenes — servers, logic, and data.

notes.title: Database
notes.description: Where apps store their data permanently. SQL vs NoSQL and when to use which.
